title: Cabinet Clears 78-Day Diwali Bonus for 11.4 Lakh Railway Employees
excerpt: The Rs 2,009.61 crore Productivity Linked Bonus pays up to Rs 17,951 per eligible employee — capped by a Rs 7,000 salary ceiling, dating to 2014-15, that unions want raised to Rs 18,000.
body:
• The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved a Productivity Linked Bonus equal to 78 days' wages for about 11,40,770 non-gazetted railway employees, at a total cost of Rs 2,009.61 crore.
  • Each eligible employee will receive up to Rs 17,951 — the maximum is set by a notional salary ceiling of Rs 7,000 a month that has not changed since 2014-15.
  • Employee unions want the ceiling raised to Rs 18,000, which would lift the maximum payout to roughly Rs 46,184; the Cabinet did not change it.
  • The bonus follows a record year: Indian Railways loaded 1,670 million tonnes of freight and carried nearly 7.41 billion passengers in 2025-26.

More than 11.4 lakh railway employees will receive a bonus equal to 78 days' wages ahead of the festival season, after the Union Cabinet approved a Productivity Linked Bonus (PLB) payout of Rs 2,009.61 crore on Wednesday. The decision, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, covers 11,40,770 eligible non-gazetted employees, according to the Cabinet release reported by Upstox with PTI inputs.

Who Gets What

The maximum payable to an eligible employee is Rs 17,951 for the 78 days. The bonus reaches the workforce that runs the network day to day: track maintainers, loco pilots, train managers (guards), station masters, supervisors, technicians, technician helpers, pointsmen, ministerial staff and other Group C employees. Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw called it a Diwali gift for employees who work around the clock on tracks, in locomotives and in workshops while others celebrate with their families.

https://x.com/DDNewslive/status/2110446524585115981

"This bonus is a Diwali gift for the hardworking railway employees who work tirelessly day and night."

— Ashwini Vaishnaw, Union Railway Minister

A Bonus Tied to a Record Year

The PLB, paid every year before the Durga Puja and Dussehra holidays, is designed as an incentive linked to the Railways' performance rather than a flat ex-gratia payment. The Cabinet cited a strong 2025-26: Indian Railways loaded a record 1,670 million tonnes of cargo and carried nearly 7.41 billion passengers. The scheme itself dates to 1979, and the 78-day figure matches the level approved in recent years.

The Ceiling Staff Want Changed

The one number that did not move is the one unions care about most. The bonus is calculated on a notional monthly salary ceiling of Rs 7,000, unchanged since 2014-15, which is why 78 days of "wages" produces a maximum of Rs 17,951 rather than a sum based on actual pay. Employee organisations, including the Indian Railway Technical Supervisors Association, have demanded the ceiling be raised to about Rs 18,000; on the unions' arithmetic that would take the maximum payout to roughly Rs 46,184. This year's approval, as Dainik Jagran's report notes, includes no change to the calculation limit. Staff have also been warned by the Railway Board about a forged letter circulating with a much larger bonus figure; employees have been told to rely only on official Railway Board and ministry communications.

Why It Matters

Indian Railways is one of the world's largest employers, and the PLB is among the biggest single pre-festival disbursements in the public sector. For the diaspora, it is also a familiar line item: millions of families have a relative on the railway payroll, and the festival-season payout is part of the Diwali economy — remittances, gifting and travel spending all move with it. The trains those employees run will carry a large share of India's Diwali travel rush in the coming days.
